I don't have any issues with GMO's but they should be labelled for people that have an issue with them. I don't really see this passing, though.

The problem with trying to label GMO foods is that it is hard to define what should or should not be defined as "Genetically Modified". Should grafting or hybridization or cross breeding, practices that started thousands of years ago, be defined as "Genetically Modified"?

One of the most popular methods used when producing "Organic" labeled foods found in places like trader joes and whole foods is mutagenesis. Mutagenesis is the process in plant breeding where random mutations are induced in plant DNA using chemicals or radiation. Scientists have been doing this in the laboratories since the 1930s. We now regularly eat more than 2,000 mutagenically created foods, including such organic favorites as Ruby Red grapefruits and versions of wheat used to make organic Italian pasta–all developed over years of laboratory research.

The other problem is that there is no way to detect a difference in sugar from genetically altered sugar beets than sugar from other sources. The chemical structure of organic chemical byproducts like sugar are the same no matter their source.

The MARS corporation, the 6th largest comapany in the US most popularly known for their various lines of candy, are lobbying for labeling GMOs as a way to push profits for their brand of "Seeds of Change" seeds derived from processes of mutagenesis. It's their way of trying to use government regulation as a corporate "weapon".
